subject: Observability onboarding: dashboards, traces & alert routing (Cloudmarq)
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudmarq.io>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cloudmarq.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Observability kickoff — Cloudmarq implementation

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re gearing up to start the Redwood onboarding next week and wanted to share our high-level needs so the implementation plan can include the right milestones. Top priorities for us:

- Dashboards: latency & p95 per model route, token-cost correlation, token-level billing split by environment
- Tracing hooks: distributed traces from our API gateway into Redwood calls + example spans and attributes we expect to see
- Error taxonomy & alerting: we want clear severities for model failures vs infra (GPU OOM, kv-cache misses, model fallback)
- Runbooks & on-call routing: who to page for critical production failures and our SLA expectations

I attached our infra requirements spreadsheet (Cloudmarq_infra_requirements.xlsx) and included a Drive link with sample dashboards we’d like to mirror.

Can we schedule a 90-minute implementation planning session — proposed agenda: data/credentials, tracing schema, dashboards mapping, alert routing, SSO/KMS items, and timeline + owner assignments.

Available windows for our team: Wed 7/14 10–12 PT or Thu 7/15 9–11 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth handoff.

Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, Cloudmarq
jordan.ellis@cloudmarq.io
Attachments: Cloudmarq_infra_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudmarq.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff — Cloudmarq implementation

Jordan — thanks for the summary and the spreadsheet, super helpful. We can absolutely cover all of that in an implementation planning session. Proposed plan below and initial owner assignments:

Agenda (90m):
1) Credentials & data flows (10m) — Aisha
2) Tracing schema & example spans (20m) — Monica
3) Dashboards mapping & KPIs (20m) — Ben
4) Alert taxonomy & routing (20m) — Monica + Ben
5) Runbooks + rollout timeline (15m) — Aisha

Owners: Ben Carter (dashboards/visualization + token-cost mapping), Monica Patel (tracing hooks, spans, alert taxonomy), me for runbooks and rollout schedule.

We can take Wed 7/14 10:30–12:00 PT if that works for you (I blocked 10:30–12:00 PT tentative). If you prefer Thu 7/15 we can do 9:00–10:30 PT. Please confirm attendees and which time you prefer.

I’ll bring a runbook template and a short checklist for required IAM/SSO access.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudmarq.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff — Cloudmarq implementation

Quick follow-up from me with a pre-meeting checklist so we can hit the ground running:

- Dashboard inputs I’ll need: sample token billing export, per-route latency logs (raw), and desired groupings (by env, route, model).
- Preferred visualization platform (Redwood Console metrics + Grafana?). If Grafana, we’ll provide a dashboard json.
- Any existing alert thresholds you already use (p95, error-rate %) so we don’t duplicate.

If you can drop the sample token export and a small set (10–20 rows) of route latency logs, I’ll draft a dashboard mapping before the call.

Ben Carter
Principal Observability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cloudmarq.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudmarq.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff — Cloudmarq implementation

Thanks Ben — attaching a small export of sample traces and a trimmed token billing CSV (sample-traces.ndjson).

Notes:
- We use an in-house gateway that injects: trace_id, span_id, route_name, model_variant, env (staging/prod).
- We’d like traces to show Redwood-request-id and token counts as attributes where possible.
- Retention: currently 90 days for traces; we’d like guidance on cost vs retention tradeoffs (happy to review Redwood Optimize recommendations).
- SSO: we use Okta. We’ll need SAML-based onboarding for Redwood Console (can you send SSO metadata pointers).

Credentials: I’ll send a separate email with a temporary service account key and a read-only Grafana link for the dashboard skeleton.

Alicia Park
Director, Infrastructure, Cloudmarq
Attachments: sample-traces.ndjson, cloudmarq-token-export.csv (csv)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@cloudmarq.io>, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff — Observability schema + runbook draft

On Tue, Jul 13, 2027 at 08:13 AM Alicia Park <alicia.park@cloudmarq.io> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — attaching a small export of sample traces and a trimmed token billing CSV (sample-traces.ndjson).
>
> Notes:
> - We use an in-house gateway that injects: trace_id, span_id, route_name, model_variant, env (staging/prod).
> - We’d like traces to show Redwood-request-id and token counts as attributes where possible.
> - Retention: currently 90 days for traces; we’d like guidance on cost vs retention tradeoffs (happy to review Redwood Optimize recommendations).
> - SSO: we use Okta. We’ll need SAML-based onboarding for Redwood Console (can you send SSO metadata pointers).

Thanks — this is perfect context. I reviewed the sample and sketched a tracing schema that maps your gateway attributes to Redwood span fields. Attached is a short runbook draft (redwood-observability-runbook-draft.md) that includes:

- Tracing schema (required attributes, naming conventions)
- Dashboards mapping (p95, p50, qps, token-cost per route)
- Error taxonomy (sev-1: model crash / fallback to smaller model; sev-2: high error-rate or repeated timeouts; sev-3: degraded performance / kv-cache thrash)
- Alert routing: sev-1 -> on-call SRE (pager duty), sev-2 -> primary app owner + CS escalation to Redwood, sev-3 -> email+slack digest
- Playbook steps for common incidents (OOM, model-mismatch, certificate rotation)

Action items before the call:
1) Alicia to share temporary service account and Grafana read-only link (you mentioned you will).
2) Jordan to confirm on-call rotation (names + escalation hours).
3) Cloudmarq to confirm retention policy decision (90 days vs 30/7 for hot traces).

I can walk through the runbook and alert routing during the workshop and we’ll capture decisions in the Jira ticket ENG-9876.

Monica Patel
Senior Observability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-observability-runbook-draft.md (md)
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@cloudmarq.io>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff — Cloudmarq implementation

Perfect — thanks everyone. Wed 7/14 10:30–12:00 PT works; Alicia will send the service account and Grafana link by EOD today.

We’ll confirm on-call rotation (two SREs on weekdays, one weekend) by tomorrow morning. Looking forward to the workshop and the draft runbook — I’ll add ENG-9876 to our internal tracking.

Jordan
